answer: For a poll on a raven and falcon voyage mural, applicants commit to hashed choices before a public random draw selects 10 commitments. The server counts selected ballots only when their revealed choices and salts match their commitments; it rejects failures and unselected ballots. Filling 10 of 100 commitments gives an expected one selection, costing submission effort. Fake commitments can crowd out voters, and unrevealed choices are lost.
